name: Asymptotic Analysis Basics
description: Fundamental framework for evaluating algorithm efficiency using Big-O, Omega, and Theta notations. Provides mathematical rigor for comparing growth rates of functions.
common_pitfalls: Confusing worst-case performance with upper bounds

name: Loop Invariants
description: Technique for proving the correctness of iterative algorithms by establishing a property that holds before and after each iteration. Ensures the algorithm achieves its desired post-condition.
common_pitfalls: Failing to maintain the invariant during the final transition step

name: Mathematical Induction
description: Proof technique used to establish the truth of an infinite sequence of statements, heavily relied upon in both loop invariants and recursive algorithm analysis. Forms the logical backbone of algorithm correctness proofs.
common_pitfalls: Assuming the inductive hypothesis for the base case

name: Recursion Fundamentals
description: Programming and mathematical paradigm where a function calls itself to solve smaller instances of the same problem. Requires a well-defined base case to prevent infinite execution.
common_pitfalls: Omitting or incorrectly defining the base case

name: Recursion Trees
description: Graphical representation of the costs incurred by recursive function calls at each level of execution. Used to visualize and sum the total work done by divide-and-conquer algorithms.
common_pitfalls: Miscalculating the number of leaves or the branching factor

name: Master Theorem
description: Formulaic method for solving recurrence relations common in divide-and-conquer algorithms. Quickens the asymptotic analysis of algorithms without requiring deep expansion steps.
common_pitfalls: Applying the theorem when the recurrence is not in the standard form

name: Advanced Algorithm Verification
description: Synthesis of loop invariants and inductive proofs to guarantee absolute correctness and complexity bounds for complex computational routines. Combines structural and asymptotic properties.
